comments.body: Thanks for the bug report! I'll take a look.

Update: On ToM I am now see this assertion failure for the full model
```
iree-compile: iree/compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/Common/GPUDistributeSharedMemoryCopy.cpp:167: SmallVector<linalg::ProcInfo> mlir::iree_compiler::getIds(OpBuilder &, Location, ArrayRef<Range>, Value): Assertion `offset && stride && size' failed.
```
and on this branch: https://github.com/antiagainst/iree/tree/use-dummy-set-for-builtin I am seeing
```
iree-compile: iree/compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/Common/GPUDistributeSharedMemoryCopy.cpp:188: auto mlir::iree_compiler::distributeTransferRead(func::FuncOp, Value, int64_t, const llvm::SmallDenseSet<VectorTransferOpInterface> &)::(anonymous class)::operator()(vector::TransferReadOp) const: Assertion `numThreads % threads == 0' failed.

```
The GPU error was fixed in top of master
@antiagainst Could this be some sort of missing barrier (?) since this doesn't happen when each dispatch is run separately.  resnet50 also works ok when lowered via Torch

There is an issue in the deduction of whether shared memory copy can be vectorized. So it's actually hitting assertions like the above messages. (In the binaries shipped with Python it's release build so they are gone and causing incorrect code generated.) I've uploaded #10468 to fix this.

issue.body:
### What happened?

Results for Resnet50 from MHLO on AMD+Vulkan are incorrect
```
       AssertionError: 
       Not equal to tolerance rtol=0.01, atol=0.001
       
       Mismatched elements: 184 / 1000 (18.4%)
       Max absolute difference: 0.12715043
       Max relative difference: 153.15282
        x: array([[2.305082e-05, 1.501763e-05, 2.055669e-06, 3.944536e-05,
               5.038393e-05, 9.031575e-06, 3.405565e-06, 5.351820e-05,
               2.354615e-05, 4.853825e-05, 7.850219e-06, 3.994784e-05,...
        y: array([[9.942157e-04, 6.844919e-04, 3.696360e-05, 6.494486e-05,
               3.446408e-04, 1.853007e-04, 5.463219e-04, 2.600181e-04,
               1.915029e-03, 5.370981e-04, 1.132972e-04, 4.064231e-04,...
```
and also inconsistent
```
       AssertionError: 
       Not equal to tolerance rtol=0.01, atol=0.001
       
       Mismatched elements: 169 / 1000 (16.9%)
       Max absolute difference: 0.12716901
       Max relative difference: 113.1847
        x: array([[2.305082e-05, 1.501763e-05, 2.055669e-06, 3.944536e-05,
               5.038393e-05, 9.031575e-06, 3.405565e-06, 5.351820e-05,
               2.354615e-05, 4.853825e-05, 7.850219e-06, 3.994784e-05,...
        y: array([[1.572465e-03, 6.260098e-04, 1.890697e-05, 5.350529e-05,
               3.314842e-04, 2.941036e-04, 9.479997e-04, 2.177179e-04,
               1.032550e-03, 2.511301e-04, 7.159870e-05, 2.720399e-04,...
```

Note that the results are correct for CPU/NVIDIA Vulkan. Adding `--iree-flow-trace-dispatch-tensors` shows that the dispatches for Vulkan and CPU match up until `forward_dispatch_37_conv_2d_nhwc_hwcf_1x14x14x256x3x3x256` where we see strange output
```
=== forward_dispatch_37::forward_dispatch_37_conv_2d_nhwc_hwcf_1x14x14x256x3x3x256 outputs ===
1x14x14x256xf32=[[[0 0 0 6.27034E+35 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 3.20595E+35 0 0 1.57074E+36 ...]]]
```
and ultimately instead of being slightly incorrect the results are all NaN.
```
=== forward_dispatch_77::forward_dispatch_77_generic_1x1000 outputs ===
1x1000xf32=[-NAN -NAN -NAN -NAN -NAN -NAN -NAN -NAN -NAN -NAN -NAN -NAN -NAN -NAN ... ]
```

If we then take that dispatch and compile + run it in isolation with random arguments
```
#map0 = affine_map<(d0, d1, d2, d3) -> (d0, d1, d2, d3)>
#map1 = affine_map<(d0, d1, d2, d3) -> (d3)>
module attributes {torch.debug_module_name = "BadConv"} {
  func.func @forward_dispatch_37_conv_2d_nhwc_hwcf_1x14x14x256x3x3x256(%arg0: tensor<1x16x16x256xf32>, %arg1: tensor<3x3x256x256xf32>, %arg2: tensor<256xf32>, %arg3: tensor<256xf32>, %arg4: tensor<256xf32>, %arg5: tensor<256xf32>) -> tensor<1x14x14x256xf32> {
    %cst = arith.constant 0.000000e+00 : f32
    %cst_0 = arith.constant 1.001000e-05 : f32
    %6 = linalg.init_tensor [1, 14, 14, 256] : tensor<1x14x14x256xf32>
    %7 = linalg.fill ins(%cst : f32) outs(%6 : tensor<1x14x14x256xf32>) -> tensor<1x14x14x256xf32>
    %8 = linalg.conv_2d_nhwc_hwcf {dilations = dense<1> : tensor<2xi64>, strides = dense<1> : tensor<2xi64>} ins(%arg0, %arg1 : tensor<1x16x16x256xf32>, tensor<3x3x256x256xf32>) outs(%7 : tensor<1x14x14x256xf32>) -> tensor<1x14x14x256xf32>
    %9 = linalg.generic {indexing_maps = [#map0, #map1, #map1, #map1, #map1, #map0], iterator_types = ["parallel", "parallel", "parallel", "parallel"]} ins(%8, %arg2, %arg3, %arg4, %arg5 : tensor<1x14x14x256xf32>, tensor<256xf32>, tensor<256xf32>, tensor<256xf32>, tensor<256xf32>) outs(%6 : tensor<1x14x14x256xf32>) {
    ^bb0(%arg7: f32, %arg8: f32, %arg9: f32, %arg10: f32, %arg11: f32, %arg12: f32):
      %10 = arith.addf %arg10, %cst_0 : f32
      %11 = math.sqrt %10 : f32
      %12 = arith.addf %arg7, %cst : f32
      %13 = arith.subf %12, %arg8 : f32
      %14 = arith.mulf %13, %arg9 : f32
      %15 = arith.divf %14, %11 : f32
      %16 = arith.addf %15, %arg11 : f32
      %17 = arith.maxf %16, %cst : f32
      linalg.yield %17 : f32
    } -> tensor<1x14x14x256xf32>
    return %9 : tensor<1x14x14x256xf32>
  }
}
```
We find that it gives matching results with cpu
```
cpu
EXEC @forward_dispatch_37_conv_2d_nhwc_hwcf_1x14x14x256x3x3x256
result[0]: hal.buffer_view
1x14x14x256xf32=[[[899.163 268.832 54.746 737.203 898.427 ... ]]]

gpu
EXEC @forward_dispatch_37_conv_2d_nhwc_hwcf_1x14x14x256x3x3x256
result[0]: hal.buffer_view
1x14x14x256xf32=[[[899.163 268.832 54.746 737.203 898.427 ... ]]]
```


### Steps to reproduce your issue

To execute the full model
```
wget https://storage.googleapis.com/shark_tank/latest/resnet50_tf/resnet50_tf.mlir

iree-compile resnet50_tf.mlir --iree-llvm-target-cpu-features=host --iree-mhlo-demote-i64-to-i32=false --iree-flow-demote-i64-to-i32 -iree-vulkan-target-triple=rdna1-6900xt-linux --iree-stream-resource-index-bits=64 --iree-vm-target-index-bits=64 --iree-input-type=mhlo --iree-hal-target-backends=vulkan-spirv -o resnet50_tf.vmfb

iree-run-module --device=vulkan --entry_function=forward --function_input=@inputs.npy --module_file=resnet50_tf.vmfb
```
and add `--iree-flow-trace-dispatch-tensors` to get NaN output. The input file can be retrieved with
```
wget https://storage.googleapis.com/shark_tank/latest/resnet50_tf/inputs.npz
```
Then converted with
```python
import numpy as np

input = np.load("inputs.npz")
np.save("inputs.npy", input['arr_0'])
```

To run the extracted conv dispatch use
```
iree-compile badconv/bad_conv.mlir --iree-llvm-target-cpu-features=host --iree-mhlo-demote-i64-to-i32=false --iree-flow-demote-i64-to-i32 -iree-vulkan-target-triple=rdna1-6900xt-linux --iree-stream-resource-index-bits=64 --iree-vm-target-index-bits=64 --iree-hal-target-backends=vulkan-spirv -o bad_conv.vmfb

iree-run-module --device=vulkan --entry_function=forward_dispatch_37_conv_2d_nhwc_hwcf_1x14x14x256x3x3x256 --function_input=@badconv/arg0.npy  --function_input=@badconv/arg1.npy --function_input=@badconv/arg2.npy --function_input=@badconv/arg3.npy --function_input=@badconv/arg4.npy --function_input=@badconv/arg5.npy --module_file=bad_conv.vmfb
```

and arguments can be generated with
```python
import torch
import numpy as np

arg0 = torch.rand(1, 16, 16, 256)
arg1 = torch.rand(3, 3, 256, 256)
arg2 = torch.rand(256)
arg3 = torch.rand(256)
arg4 = torch.rand(256)
arg5 = torch.rand(256)

np.save("badconv/arg0.npy", arg0.numpy())
np.save("badconv/arg1.npy", arg1.numpy())
np.save("badconv/arg2.npy", arg2.numpy())
np.save("badconv/arg3.npy", arg3.numpy())
np.save("badconv/arg4.npy", arg4.numpy())
np.save("badconv/arg5.npy", arg5.numpy())

```

### What component(s) does this issue relate to?

_No response_

### Version information

the iree-compiler and iree-runtime versions are
```
iree-compiler==20220908.69
iree-runtime==20220908.69
```
amdgpu from upstream 6.0.0-rc4 kernel with latest amdvulkan drivers built from source.

_No response_

issue.body:
When there are no enough remaining threads for a particular shape dimension size, try to use all remaining threads. But we still need to make sure all work can be distributed to these threads evenly.

Also added some debug prints in GPUDistributeSharedMemoryCopyPass to make debugging easier.

Fixes https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/10447
